intro.text: Kalinga University promotes inclusive economic growth by providing quality education, skill development, internships, entrepreneurship opportunities, and industry-oriented training. The University encourages innovation, employability, startups, and professional development through industry collaborations, placement initiatives, incubation support, and career guidance. These initiatives enhance students’ skills, create employment opportunities, and contribute to sustainable livelihoods and regional economic development.

sections.title: 8.1 Research on Economic Growth and Employment

blocks.text: 8.1.1 Decent Work and Economic Growth: CiteScore

Kalinga University’s research portfolio contributes to SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth through scholarly research addressing sustainable economic development, employment generation, industrial innovation, entrepreneurship, and productivity. The portfolio comprises 136 Scopus-indexed publications with 328 citations, demonstrating research visibility and academic engagement. All publications have received citations, reflecting consistent scholarly reach. The Field-Weighted Citation Impact (FWCI) of 1.12 indicates citation performance 12% above the global average, supporting knowledge creation relevant to inclusive and sustainable economic growth.
8.1.2 Decent Work and Economic Growth: Publications
SDG 8 – Decent Work and Economic Growth: Research Output (2020–2025)

During 2020–2025, research aligned with SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth demonstrates a strong focus on smart technologies, sustainable energy, industrial transformation, agriculture, finance, and digital commerce. As shown in the research analysis, 20 major thematic areas were identified, accounting for a total of 270 research-paper occurrences. The highest contributions were observed in Smart City (24), Renewable Energies (23), Smart Power Grids (19), Investments (18), Industry 4.0 (18), Smart Grid (17), Smart Manufacturing (16), Sales (16), and Commerce (16). Other significant areas include Smart Agriculture and Precision Agriculture (14 each), Financial Markets and Costs (13 each), Solar Power Generation (11), Economics (8), Urban Growth, Smart Farming and Decentralized Finance (7 each), E-Commerce (5), and Stock Market Prediction (4). Collectively, these research areas contribute to technological innovation, productivity, sustainable economic development, digital transformation, financial inclusion, and employment-oriented growth, supporting the objectives of SDG 8.

These research themes demonstrate the University's contribution to technological innovation, sustainable infrastructure, digital transformation, financial development, and employment-oriented economic growth under SDG 8.

Kalinga University, Raipur, is committed to fair, transparent, and inclusive employment practices that promote employee welfare and professional growth. The University follows merit-based recruitment, an Equal Opportunity Policy, and non-discriminatory employment practices. Its employment framework encompasses a structured salary system, increment and performance appraisal policies, leave provisions, and applicable employment benefits. A feedback and complaints redressal mechanism supports employees in raising workplace concerns and seeking appropriate resolution. The University also encourages professional development through training programmes and capacity-building initiatives while striving to maintain a safe, respectful, and supportive work environment. These practices promote employee satisfaction, institutional accountability, and SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth.
8.2.1 Employment Practice Living Wage
Salary Structure & Equal Pay

Kalinga University, Raipur, follows a structured and transparent salary framework based on employees’ qualifications, experience, designation, responsibilities, and applicable institutional norms. The University promotes equal pay for equal work, ensuring fairness, non-discrimination, and equal employment opportunities irrespective of gender. Salary revisions and increments are considered in accordance with institutional policies, performance evaluations, and applicable regulations. This approach supports employee satisfaction, financial stability, and a fair and inclusive workplace.
Benefits for Employees

Kalinga University provides employee benefits in accordance with institutional policies and applicable statutory requirements. These may include leave entitlements, holidays, professional development opportunities, and other admissible employment benefits. The University promotes employee well-being through a supportive work environment, grievance redressal mechanisms, and appropriate channels for feedback and complaints. These measures aim to maintain a healthy work-life balance, strengthen employee engagement, and foster a culture of mutual respect, trust, and organizational commitment.
Other Academic Incentives

Kalinga University encourages faculty members to enhance their academic and professional contributions through research, innovation, teaching excellence, and continuous professional development. Academic incentives and recognition may be provided in accordance with University policies for research publications, patents, funded research projects, participation in conferences, Faculty Development Programmes (FDPs), and other scholarly achievements. The University also encourages faculty members to pursue higher qualifications, undertake interdisciplinary research, collaborate with industry, and contribute to academic quality enhancement, thereby strengthening institutional performance and educational excellence.
8.2.2 Employment Practice Unions
Employment Welfare at Kalinga University, Raipur

Kalinga University, Raipur, is committed to promoting employee welfare through a structured Human Resource (HR) Manual that emphasizes fairness, inclusivity, professional development, and employee well-being. The University provides a range of welfare measures designed to support the personal and professional needs of its teaching and non-teaching staff.

The University’s Leave Policy provides various leave facilities, including casual leave, earned/medical leave, special leave, maternity leave, paternity leave, semester breaks, and compensatory duty leave, subject to applicable eligibility conditions and university rules. These provisions support work-life balance and help employees manage personal and family responsibilities.

Under its Employee Gift Policy, eligible confirmed employees may receive gifts on specified occasions, including their own marriage, the birth of a child, and their child’s marriage. The Interest-Free Loan Policy offers eligible employees financial assistance for specified needs, such as medical emergencies involving themselves or eligible family members and children’s education, subject to management approval and repayment conditions.

Kalinga University also encourages career progression through its Annual Increment Policy, Special Increment Policy, and promotion provisions. Faculty performance is assessed through academic contributions, research publications, professional development, and institutional responsibilities. Eligible employees may receive increments or promotions for specified qualifications and achievements. The University’s Research, Consultancy and Intellectual Property Rights Policy, Seed Money Policy, and Travel Policy further support research engagement and official professional activities.

Additionally, the Equal Opportunity Policy promotes dignity, fairness, inclusion, and freedom from discrimination, harassment, bullying, and victimisation. The HR Manual also establishes grievance-redressal mechanisms, including the Internal Complaints Committee and University Grievance Redressal Committee.
Through these policies, Kalinga University strives to foster a supportive, equitable, and professionally enriching workplace.

The HR Manual of Kalinga University covers employee welfare measures and other employment practices, including leave facilities, employee benefits, increments, promotions, equal opportunity, grievance redressal, and professional development. It provides a structured framework for managing employee-related matters and promoting fairness, inclusivity, well-being, and professional growth among teaching and non-teaching staff. Through these policies and procedures, the University aims to maintain a supportive, transparent, and equitable working environment.

blocks.text: 8.2.3 Employment Policy on Discrimination

Kalinga University is committed to providing a fair, inclusive, and respectful workplace through its Employment Non-Discrimination Policy. The policy promotes equal employment opportunities and prohibits discrimination in recruitment, employment, and professional development. It encourages a culture of dignity, fairness, and mutual respect for all employees, irrespective of gender or other protected characteristics, in accordance with applicable laws and institutional regulations.
This policy has been in effect since the academic year 2015–16, and the next review scheduled for the academic year 2027–28.

blocks.text: 8.2.4 Employment Policy: Modern Slavery

Kalinga University is committed to preventing modern slavery, forced labour, human trafficking, and all forms of workplace exploitation. The Policy Against Modern Slavery in Employment promotes a safe, ethical, respectful, and inclusive working environment, safeguarding employees’ dignity, freedom, and fair treatment. The policy has been in effect since the academic year 2015–16 and is scheduled for its next review in 2027–28 to ensure continued relevance, effective implementation, and compliance with applicable laws and institutional regulations.

blocks.text: 8.2.5 Employment Practice Equivalent Rights Outsourcing

Kalinga University is committed to promoting equivalent rights and fair employment practices for outsourced personnel. The University aims to ensure that outsourced employees are treated with dignity, fairness, and respect, without discrimination. Employment-related practices are guided by applicable rules, contractual conditions, and institutional procedures. The University encourages a safe, inclusive, and respectful working environment, supporting equitable treatment and responsible employment practices for outsourced staff alongside its regular workforce.

blocks.text: 8.2.6 Employment Policy Pay Scale Equity

Kalinga University is committed to promoting pay scale equity through fair, transparent, and structured compensation practices. Salary determination is guided by applicable university policies, employee designations, qualifications, experience, responsibilities, and relevant regulatory norms, wherever applicable. The University aims to ensure equitable remuneration, consistency in compensation, and equal opportunities for career progression. Through established HR procedures, it strives to maintain fairness, recognize employee contributions, and foster a supportive and inclusive working environment.

blocks.text: 8.2.7 Tracking Pay Scale for Gender Equity

Kalinga University maintains an institutional Human Resource (HR) Manual and related procedures that provide a structured framework for managing employee remuneration and employment conditions. The University is committed to fair compensation, equal opportunity, and equitable treatment of male and female employees. Salary structures are determined by relevant factors, including designation, qualifications, experience, responsibilities, and applicable policies.

As part of its commitment to gender equity, the University may review remuneration data across male and female faculty and staff categories to identify potential pay disparities. Where unexplained differences are identified, appropriate reviews and corrective measures may be undertaken in accordance with university policies and applicable regulations.

These practices support the University’s commitment to SDG 5 – Gender Equality and SDG 8 – Decent Work and Economic Growth, promoting fair employment, equal opportunities, and gender-equitable remuneration.

8.2.8 Employment Practice: Appeal Process

Kalinga University, Raipur, is committed to maintaining a fair, transparent, and inclusive working environment through an established grievance redressal and appeal mechanism. The University provides channels for employees to raise concerns and seek review of workplace matters, including harassment, discrimination, professional conduct, employment conditions, and other service-related issues. Dedicated committees and designated authorities address grievances in accordance with applicable university policies and procedures, ensuring impartial consideration and appropriate resolution.

The University also utilizes its ERP System to facilitate the submission, recording, tracking, and follow-up of employee grievances, where applicable. This system supports systematic documentation, improved communication, and greater transparency in the grievance-handling process. Employees can seek clarification, submit concerns, and pursue appropriate review through the prescribed institutional channels. These practices reflect the University’s commitment to employee welfare, accountability, and fair employment practices, supporting SDG 8 – Decent Work and Economic Growth by promoting a respectful, safe, and equitable workplace.

The policy promotes dignity, equality, and non-discrimination, with mechanisms for reporting and addressing complaints through designated committees and institutional procedures. The University strives to ensure confidentiality, fairness, and appropriate action in accordance with applicable policies and regulations.

blocks.text: 8.2.9 Employment Practice: Labor Rights

Kalinga University, Raipur, is committed to respecting the labor rights of its employees and promoting fair, inclusive, and respectful employment practices in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, and institutional policies.

The University’s Human Resource (HR) Manual and related employment procedures provide a framework for protecting employee rights, ensuring equitable treatment, and enabling staff members to raise employment-related concerns through established grievance redressal mechanisms. The University strives to maintain a workplace free from discrimination, unfair treatment, harassment, and retaliation for exercising legitimate employment rights. University encourages constructive communication between employees and the administration and supports fair opportunities for staff participation in recognized employee representation mechanisms, where applicable. These principles contribute to responsible human resource management, employee welfare, and a positive working environment.

Through these commitments, the University supports SDG 8 – Decent Work and Economic Growth, particularly the promotion of decent working conditions, workers’ rights, equal opportunity, and fair employment practices.

Kalinga University, Raipur, is committed to protecting employee rights and promoting a fair, inclusive, and supportive working environment through its institutional policies on labour rights and employee welfare. The University has established policies such as the Maternity Leave and Support Policy, Paternity Leave and Support Policy, and Policy for the Protection of Individuals Reporting Discrimination. These policies provide an institutional framework for supporting employees during important family-related circumstances and encouraging the reporting of discrimination without fear of unfair treatment. They reflect the University’s commitment to employee well-being, gender equity, dignity, and non-discrimination. Through these measures, Kalinga University strives to strengthen responsible employment practices, support work–life balance, and promote a respectful workplace for its staff. These initiatives align with SDG 5 – Gender Equality and SDG 8 – Decent Work and Economic Growth, supporting inclusive employment and the protection of employees’ legitimate rights.

blocks.text: Employee Training and Development
Facilitating Learning and Development at Kalinga University

Programs for Professional Development: Kalinga University, Raipur, promotes continuous learning and skill enhancement among its teaching and non-teaching staff through Faculty Development Programmes (FDPs), workshops, seminars, conferences, and training sessions. These initiatives help employees update their knowledge, strengthen professional competencies, adopt innovative practices, and improve workplace effectiveness, supporting SDG 8 – Decent Work and Economic Growth.

Mentoring: The University encourages professional growth through mentoring, guidance, and collaborative learning opportunities. These initiatives support new and existing employees in adapting to institutional responsibilities, developing relevant skills, improving performance, and pursuing career advancement. Mentoring also promotes knowledge sharing, teamwork, and a supportive working environment.

Performance Management: Kalinga University follows institutional procedures for employee performance assessment and professional development. Performance reviews, feedback, and evaluation of assigned responsibilities help identify strengths and areas for improvement. These processes encourage accountability, recognize employee contributions, and support continuous improvement in teaching, research, administration, and other institutional activities, contributing to productive employment and organizational development.

8.4.1 Proportion of Students with Work Placements

The proportion of students with work placements at Kalinga University reflects the University’s commitment to enhancing graduate employability and career readiness. Through its Training and Placement Cell, the University facilitates campus recruitment, industry collaborations, internships, career counselling, and skill-development programmes to prepare students for employment opportunities aligned with their academic qualifications and industry requirements.
Total No. of Students Year 2024-25: Total 1521

Kalinga University demonstrated a positive placement trend from 2020–21 to 2024–25, with student placements increasing from 1,438 to 1,521. Although placements declined to 1,073 in 2021–22, they recovered steadily in subsequent years, reaching the highest figure of 1,521 in 2024–25, reflecting the University’s commitment to graduate employability.

Understanding Intellectual Property Rights: Participants understood the key concepts and types of intellectual property rights (patents, trademarks, copyrights, designs) relevant to innovation and entrepreneurship. IPR Protection and Management: Students acquired knowledge to identify, protect, and manage intellectual property assets, including knowledge of patent filing and trademark registration processes. Legal and Ethical Awareness: Learners develop awareness of the legal and ethical considerations in IPR, including recognizing infringement and respecting third-party intellectual property.

They understood the application of biotechnology and research principles, explored sustainable agricultural innovations, and recognized the role of quality seeds in food security, climate resilience, improved productivity, teamwork, communication, and professional skill development.

Workshop on “Entrepreneurship and Careers in Forensic Science”

Students gained awareness of emerging entrepreneurial opportunities within forensic and allied sectors. The session enhanced understanding of professional skills, innovation, and research-driven career growth. Participants learned about start-up possibilities, private consultancy, and industrial collaborations in forensic science. The workshop bridged the gap between academic learning and real-world applications, encouraging students to think creatively and strategically. Overall, the session inspired students to build successful, independent careers while contributing to advancements in the field of forensic science.
Department of Fashion Design In Association with “USHA COMPANY”

Students will gain practical exposure to modern embroidery and quilting methods. The workshop will foster awareness about sustainable fashion practices and responsible production. It will strengthen industry–academia collaboration, improving employability and technical proficiency of students.

One of the most significant results were an enhanced understanding of entrepreneurial processes. Students were able to grasp the Lean Start-Up methodology in depth, particularly how the Build-Measure-Learn feedback loop can be applied to minimize risks and improve product-market fit. Another outcome was the real-world relevance of the session, as the examples and success stories shared by the guest speaker connected theoretical concepts with practical application. Students were able to visualize how these strategies work in different contexts, from rural technology initiatives to modern urban start-ups.
Startup India Delegation Visit and Ideathon Awareness Under IIC Activity

The awareness session successfully enhanced students’ understanding of Chhattisgarh Ideathon 2025, its objectives, and participation process. A significant number of students expressed interest in submitting innovative ideas and participating in the Ideathon. The visit strengthened the collaboration between Kalinga University and Startup Chhattisgarh, paving the way for future engagement in entrepreneurship and innovation initiatives.The delegation appreciated the infrastructure and facilities available at the Kalinga Incubation Centre (KIC), Centre of Excellence, and Centre Instrumentation Facility (CIF Lab and IIoT Section). The interaction provided valuable feedback on enhancing incubation practices, mentorship processes, and startup support systems within the university. The event created a motivating environment for students to think innovatively and pursue entrepreneurial ventures.
